newsitem.title: USA: $53,000 hotel suites unwanted, $30,000 one grabbed.
newsitem.headline: $53,000 hotel suites unwanted, $30,000 one grabbed.

text.p: Hey big spenders! A hotelier is wondering where you are and why you're not picking up its presidential inaugural special suite package -- for a mere $53,000 for four nights.

"Time is running out," Nancy McFaul of the Grand Hyatt Washington, a majestic 888-room hotel a few blocks from the White House, said of the $53,000 package, the highest price for a hotel suite for President Clinton's second inauguration.

Across town at the stately Ritz Carlton on embassy row, public relations director Ellen Gale said the hotel has signed up, after much waiting, a Texas couple for a $30,000 luxury suite package for four nights and five days. She said the couple was from Dallas and "they didn't want their name used since they thought they would be considered ostentatious."

Before the hotel nailed down the Texans, Gale fretted about the lack of big spenders for Monday's inaugural. "They (visitors) are not spending the big money this year," she sighed. But she added: "This is normal in a second inauguration."

With the Ritz Carlton's presidential suite now taken, the hotel is sold out for the inauguration, she said. The Texans will live in a luxurious 1,700-square-foot suite, get a chauffeur-driven Rolls Royce, a butler, gourmet dinner for 12, champagne and Beluga caviar and roses.

There's still room at the inn for a couple with deep pockets at any one of the Grand Hyatt's three presidential suites. The tab of $53,000 for two is symbolic since it is the 53rd presidential inaugural.
It works out to $13,250 a night. The suite ordinarily goes for $1,000 a night without all the perks thrown in.

Thursday is the deadline for reserving the suites for the four-night special beginning Friday, spokeswoman McFaul said. The reason for the deadline: Tailors and seamstresses must have time to work on custom-designed clothes for the lucky couple, who will also get a free ride to Washington and back to wherever they live in a private personal jet.

The hotel assumes that a woman is one member of any couple renting the suite, since it is offering a replica of the famous inaugural ball gown worn by Jacqueline Kennedy in 1961. The man gets a special tuxedo with all accessories.

There's also limousine service, of course, to two seats for the swearing-in ceremony at the West Front of the U.S. Capitol, and seats for the parade that follows. And the hotel is throwing in a video camera for later family viewing and a cellular phone to keep in touch with the folks back home.

For friends, the hotel will throw a no-cost reception for 30 people -- free bar, of course. The hotel suite itself has a living parlour, king-size wooden sleigh bed in the bedroom, a dining area, sauna and whirlpool.

There have also been no takers for a $9,700 special in the "vice president's quarters" at the Grand Hyatt. And there are still regular rooms available, as there are throughout town, Marie Tibor of the Washington Convention and Visitors Association said.
